Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tao —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday — really appreciate the thoughtful questions on latency and hallucination tolerance. Per our conversation, attached is a concise model shortlist with rationale tailored to Acme's invoices/QA use case. I tried to keep the tradeoffs explicit so your engineering team can evaluate speed vs. cost vs. accuracy. Quick summary below and recommended next steps.

Recommended shortlist (ranked for pilot):
- Redwood-Opt-7B-quant (recommended pilot) — best cost-to-latency balance for high-throughput ingestion. Strong on template-completion and extraction tasks when paired with our prompt set (low inference cost, quantized float16 -> ~2-3x cheaper than 13B).
- Llama-3-13B (non-quant) — higher quality on long-context reasoning and edge-case extraction, but 2-3x token cost and higher p99 latency. Good for higher-accuracy tier or fallbacks for ambiguous inputs.
- Redwood-Instruct-13B (sparsely quantized) — middle ground: better instruction-following than 7B, lower cost than full 13B with modest latency overhead.
- OpenModel-ggml-4B (edge) — for ultra-low-cost rule-approx tasks (pre-filtering & quick classification). Not recommended for final extraction.

Key benchmark notes (top-level):
- Throughput (tokens/sec): Redwood-Opt-7B-quant ~3.5k tok/s on a T4-class instance; Llama-3-13B ~1.2k tok/s.
- Latency (p50/p95 for 256-token requests): 7B-quant 110ms / 260ms; 13B non-quant 240ms / 620ms.
- Unit cost (approx): 7B-quant ~$0.60 / 1k reqs (typical short inference); 13B ~$1.8 / 1k reqs. These are rough — we can run your corpus to provide precise per-token estimates.

Attached:
- acme_model_shortlist.xlsx (breakdown by cost/latency/tests)
- demo_recording_20260401.mp4

Links:
- Model benchmarks & evals: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/acme-2026-model-benchmarks
- Shared prompt set & test inputs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-model-evals
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456789/ACME-2026-07

Next steps (proposal):
1) Quick pilot: run our 7B-quant on a 48-hour subset of your invoices (we'll provide cost estimate & sample dashboard).
2) In parallel run 13B on a 1k-sample to measure regression on edge cases (we'll produce delta reports).
3) Schedule a 90-min technical workshop with your eng team to finalize metrics for acceptance (we suggest precision/recall on extraction fields + hallucination rate).

Can you confirm which week next you prefer for the workshop? If OK, I can schedule for next Tue/Wed and loop in an SE for a short integration checklist.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

Tao / Sarah — adding a quick technical addendum to help with the procurement questions.

Dedicated vs Hosted (p95 latency):
- Hosted (shared): 7B-quant p95 ~260ms for 256-token requests; 13B p95 ~620ms. We guarantee baseline SLOs but p95 can vary during peak multi-tenant usage.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): 7B-quant p95 ~130-170ms (on A10G/RTX6000 equivalent), 13B p95 ~300-380ms depending on instance and KV cache locality. Dedicated gives consistent lower p95 and throughput headroom.

Cost estimate (very rough, will refine after sample run):
- At 10M tokens/day (~300M tokens/month):
  - 7B-quant hosted: ~$0.40 - $0.55 per 1k tokens -> ~$120k - $165k/month (hosted; bulk discounts available)
  - 7B-quant dedicated (reserved): lower per-token but plus reserved capacity fee (example: $90k/month + infra) — we can provide committed pricing once we know traffic profile.
  - 13B non-quant: ~2.5-3x the per-token compute cost depending on quantization & kernel choices.

Quality / regression notes:
- We recommend running a small evaluation harness (we call these prompt sets) of ~1k labeled samples from your historical corpus. That gives us a clear precision/recall baseline and hallucination rate. I put a starter prompt set in the Drive link (redwood suggested prompts + edge-case flags).
- For the 7B-quant, temperature and few-shot prompt engineering reduce hallucinations markedly for extraction tasks. We also suggest a lightweight reranker (Llama-3-13B) as a fallback for cases with low confidence.

Benchmarks & artifacts: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/acme-2026-model-benchmarks
Prompt set: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-model-evals

If you want, we can run a 48-hour A/B on one ingestion pipeline and return concrete p95/cost numbers + a short regression report. I'll also attach a short README with quantization caveats to the Drive folder.

Dev
